newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-DATE PUTS OFF RETIREMENT AS SELES RETIRES FROM MATCH.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-DATE PUTS OFF RETIREMENT AS SELES RETIRES FROM MATCH.

text.p: They threw a retirement party for Kimiko Date at Madison Square Garden Tuesday, but opponent Monica Seles actually did the retiring at the Chase Championship when her sore left shoulder forced her to quit.
The second-seeded Seles retired at 4-5 of the first set of their first-round match, and Date survived for at least another round at the prestigious $2 million season-ending event.

Seles, the co-world number two, called out tour trainer Kathleen Stroia during the changeover while leading 4-3 and took an injury time out while a bag of ice was applied to her shoulder, which has troubled her most of this season.

Date held serve at 15 and then broke the obviously hindered Seles at love in the next game. Seles's father, Karolj, waved a "quit" sign to his daughter as she made her way back to the sidelines and she informed the umpire she could not continue.

The 26-year-old Date, who announced earlier this autumn that she was retiring at the end of the season, will have to put off life after tennis a while longer. Her next opponent will be fifth-ranked Swiss teenager Martina Hingis.
"I can't believe this happened," Date said through an interpreter after the match. "I hope she (Seles) will recover soon."
Seles, who had beaten Date in their four previous career matches, had her disappointing season end in pain and frustration.
After winning the Australian Open to start the season, Seles tore a muscle in her left, serving shoulder and has struggled to maintain her form since.
The 22-year-old Seles lost in the quarter-finals at the French Open and in the second round at Wimbledon before clawing her way to the U.S. Open final where she lost to Steffi Graf.

At the premature retirement ceremony following the match, Date was serenaded by a Japanese children's choir from an upstate New York school, who sang "Kikyu ni Notte Do Ko made mo (Riding on the Balloon)".
"This is not the end, this is a new beginning for me," Date said in English during the on-court ceremony. "Once again, thank you, everybody and goodbye."
Date was given a set of golf clubs to help her enjoy retirement, but they will have to wait.
